Awesome!
My name's Hoagie.
Does Mrs. Washington know you wear so much makeup?
Indeed.
Like the sandwich?\255\003How quaint.
One must wear makeup when one receives the phenomenal amount of media attention that I do.\255\003It's quite likely that I'll be president soon, you know.
Yes, I expect to be chosen president unanimously.\255\003I'm VERY well connected.
As a matter of fact, I do make use of artificial teeth.\255\003I find them to be far superior to the ordinary enamel variety.
Wow, what do you brush them with?
Don't you have a problem with splinters?
Where could I get some of those?
My Uncle Henry has false teeth, too.
Well, I gotta go now.
I use a toothbrush, much like everyone else.\255\003And a bit of wood polish, of course.
Doesn't that taste awful?
Don't they make a disposable kind?
Not if you take them out, first.
Actually, I believe the proprietor of this inn is working on something like that.

I've been to WAR, boy.\255\003No one who's heard the thunder of musket fire^\255\003^smelled the sulphur from a cannon blast^\255\003^and felt the fear in the hearts of his comrades^\255\003^is going to be bothered by a little thing like--\255\003OW!!\255\003Blast it!
Well, what about termites?
Well, what about woodpeckers?
Well, what about dry rot?
Hardly.
They're rather expensive.\255\003Mine were custom-made for me by my good friend Paul Revere.
Didn't he ride a horse through town naked?
Didn't he invent 3-D glasses?
Doesn't he have a band or something?
I believe you have him confused with someone else.
Fascinating, I'm sure.
The future of our nation.
That young couple by the stump?
That young couple by the tree?
Those outhouses?
A system of free enterprise and opportunity?
No, no.
I was just admiring my reflection in the window.\255\003Striking, aren't I?
There are two sides to everything, you know that, my boy?
Wow, what issue are you contemplating?
Is it the legality of abortion?
Is it death penalty laws?
Is it victimless crimes?
What do you think, is my left side better, or my right?
Something horrible is on the rise.
Pollution?
Imperialism?
Noise control laws?
What?  What is it?
I think I'm getting a blemish.
Do you think I should be the `ecology president` or the `education president?`
I'm a big fan of education.
I think ecology is very important.
Depends on how many cherry trees you've chopped down.
I think I have to go now.
Really?\255\003How surprising.
Yes, of course, but what really matters is which one SOUNDS better.
Excellent point.
Well, I AM quite the adept tree-cutter.\255\003Men still tell tales of my youthful prowess.
Would you give me a demonstration?
I bet you've lost it.  You couldn't cut down a tree to \254\008     save your grandmother.
I think I'll go look at some trees right now.
I don't see why I should.
Lost it, have I?\255\003Why, I'd show you a thing or two, if there were a cherry tree nearby!
But as you can see, there isn't.
I only cut down CHERRY trees.\255\003Family tradition, you understand, cherries only.\255\003There's nothing out there but cedar and kumquats.
Hey, tall, dark and spiffy.\255\003My name's Hoagie.
Well, how quaint.\255\003I am, of course, Thomas Jefferson^\255\003^noted scholar, musician, horseman^\255\003^student of the sciences, member of the bar^
Oh, sure, I've heard of you, dude.
Yo, Tom.
Thomas.
So how's the time capsule going?
What's in the can, Tommy?
How goes the framing of the Constitution?
Dude, is that, like, THE Constitution?
What are you guys doing in here?
How can you let Hancock suffer like that?
Could you start a fire, please?
Has anyone ever told you you're a very snappy dresser?
Dude, I loved your work on the Declaration of Independence.
Well, later, dude.
Later, bra.
Thomas.  My name is Thomas.\255\003And this, my chubby friend, is a time capsule^
^as if you didn't know^
^filled with remembrances of our time to be revealed four hundred years hence.
Very well, now that you've provided that fine recent vintage wine.\255\003I plan to bury it this evening.
I'm sorry to say that except for my log, we haven't got a thing.
No one has brought me anything.\255\003I'm having some difficulty generating the proper spirit.
We're writing the constitution for the United States.
That's it over there?
Right now it's just A constitution, I'm afraid.\255\003We hit a slight creative block right after the preamble.\255\003That's why we've put up a suggestion box over there.
It is.\255\003Now that our esteemed leader has sparked us with his brilliant vacuum suggestion, we're really rolling!
Not so well.
We can't decide whether we should allow a free press or impose a tax.
An argument has broken out over whether we should separate church and state or legalize bingo parlors.
We can't even decide what font to use.
We're not sure if we should guarantee the right to bear arms, or if it will generate too many atrocious puns.
We don't know whether to call it the `Bill of Rights` or `Appendix A.`
I sure hope someone gives us a useful suggestion soon.
Great!\255\003George's suggestion about the vacuum cleaners really got the old creative juices flowing!
In fact, we've just given ocelots the right to vote!
We've just finished up amendment 425, which prohibits spelunking on alternate Thursdays.
Even as we speak, Hancock's polishing up his `Single Syllable Undergarment` amendment.

In a few minutes, Washington's going to present his proposal to split the government into eight branches:\255\003Executive, judicial, legislative, bronchial, atypical, Freudian, elliptical, and extra-crispy.
By tomorrow we'll have finished all 9800 amendments!
I hope they've got a good editor.
I'd love to oblige you, young man, but I can't.\255\003This is the only log, and I'm saving it for posterity.
A real man is warmed by the fires of his spirit!\255\003You should listen to Washington relate his experiences at Valley Forge, and take heed!
What?  What's going to happen later?
Why, yes.\255\003I studied at Virginia Coat and Technical, where I majored in collar theory.\255\003I was captain of the varsity cravat team.
Those are impressive credentials, Tom.
Ah, thank you.\255\003What was your favorite part?
I liked the part about Prudence.
I like those S's that look like F's.
I liked the `We the People` part.
`Prudence, indeed, will dictate that Governments long established should--`
Yeah, there's just one thing though^
Who's Prudence?
Never mind.
That's not in the Declaration of--
Say, that's not bad.\255\003Maybe we can use it.
Yo.
